record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: What is the asymptotic description of the stress field in elastic bodies whose boundary has a rounded corner, such as two straight boundary segments joined by a small-radius circular arc?

artifact.category_tag: asymptotic stress analysis at rounded corners
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega_\varepsilon \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a family of planar domains whose boundary consists of two straight segments meeting at an angle $2\alpha \in (0, 2\pi)$, joined smoothly by a circular arc of small radius $\varepsilon > 0$ (so that $\Omega_0$ has a sharp corner of opening angle $2\alpha$ at the vertex). Consider the equations of plane linear isotropic elasticity in $\Omega_\varepsilon$:
$$\mathrm{div}\,\sigma(u^\varepsilon) = 0 \text{ in } \Omega_\varepsilon, \qquad \sigma(u^\varepsilon) = \lambda (\mathrm{div}\, u^\varepsilon) I + 2\mu\, e(u^\varepsilon),$$
where $e(u)=\tfrac12(\nabla u + \nabla u^\top)$, with prescribed tractions on the straight portion of $\partial\Omega_\varepsilon$ and traction-free conditions on the rounded arc, and suitable far-field or remaining boundary data independent of $\varepsilon$.

Provide a complete asymptotic description, as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$, of the stress field $\sigma(u^\varepsilon)$ in $\Omega_\varepsilon$. In particular:

1. Construct matched asymptotic expansions consisting of an outer expansion valid away from the corner (whose leading term is the elastic solution in the limit domain $\Omega_0$ with a sharp corner, exhibiting the classical Williams-type singular expansion $\sigma \sim \sum_k c_k\, r^{\lambda_k - 1} \Phi_k(\theta)$ with exponents $\lambda_k$ determined by the corner opening angle $2\alpha$) and an inner expansion in the stretched variable $y = x/\varepsilon$, posed on the unbounded domain obtained by blow-up of the rounded corner.

2. Identify the matching conditions linking the generalized stress intensity factors $c_k$ of the sharp-corner outer solution to the inner profile, and derive the resulting maximum stress $\max |\sigma(u^\varepsilon)|$ as a function of $\varepsilon$ and of the $c_k$.

3. Give rigorous error estimates for the remainder of the two-scale expansion in appropriate Sobolev norms, uniformly in $\varepsilon$, for all opening angles $2\alpha \in (0, 2\pi)$, including the limiting crack case $2\alpha = 2\pi$.
artifact.status_search_result: The asymptotic analysis of stress near rounded corners has been extensively studied via matched asymptotic expansions, with leading-order results (linking the sharp-corner generalized stress intensity factors to the maximum stress at a small rounding radius, e.g. $\sigma_{\max}\sim K_I/\sqrt{\pi\rho}$ for cracks) well established in the engineering and applied mathematics literature. However, a fully general rigorous theory covering all opening angles, all loading modes, and providing sharp error estimates is not entirely complete; the topic is typically presented as a partially solved area with ongoing refinements.

status_evidence.title: Stresses in the region of rounded corners
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of stresses near rounded corners in elastic bodies.
status_evidence.claim: Classical analyses of stress in the region of rounded corners exist.

status_evidence.title: A generalized stress intensity factor to be applied to rounded V-shaped notches
status_evidence.snippet: When the notch tip radius is different from zero, the sharp-notch field diverges from the rounded-notch solution very near the notch; N-SIFs are used as governing parameters if root radius is sufficiently small.
status_evidence.claim: Generalized stress intensity factors for rounded V-notches partially describe the asymptotic stress field.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic solutions for almost complete frictionless contacts
status_evidence.snippet: Matched asymptotic expansions: outer field is the sharp solution with square-root singularity, inner field represents the modification due to finite rounding radius.
status_evidence.claim: Matched asymptotic expansions provide the standard methodology for rounded-corner stress asymptotics.
